title: Polynomial-chart pseudo-coherence under principal localization and base enlargement
statement: Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ be an affine scheme, let $V=D_S(a)\subseteq S$ for $a\in R$, and let $f:X\to V$ be a finite type morphism with $X$ affine [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $U=D_X(b)$ for $b\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Here $D_Z(t)$ denotes the principal open of an affine scheme $Z$ where the section $t$ is invertible. Let $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$ [def-pc-derived-category], with $E|_U=L\iota^*E$ for the open inclusion $\iota$ [def-pc-derived-pullback]. If there exist $n\geq0$ and a closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^n_V$ over $V$ such that $Ri_*E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent, then there exist $r\geq0$ and a closed immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^r_S$ over $S$ such that $Rj_*(E|_U)$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-nagata-relative-affine-space, def-pc-derived-direct-image, def-sfb-m-pseudo-coherent-complex]. No quasi-coherence assumption on $E$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09VD, lemma-localize-relative-pseudo-coherent, principal-source-open case proved explicitly by adjoining inverses

proof.text: Choose the immersion $i$ in the hypothesis. Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $B=R_a[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$; the principal-localization open immersion identifies $V=D_S(a)$ with $\operatorname{Spec}R_a$, so the affine-space chart gives $\mathbf A^n_V=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The affine description of a closed immersion gives its surjection $B\twoheadrightarrow A$. Put $C=R[t,x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ and $P=\operatorname{Spec}C=\mathbf A^{n+1}_S$. Adjoining the inverse of $a$ gives $C/(at-1)\cong B$: apply the polynomial-localization quotient statement to $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ and $a$; its localization is $R_a[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, since both have the universal property of adjoining the variables and an inverse of $a$. Thus the coefficient map is a surjection $C\twoheadrightarrow B$. It defines a closed immersion $k:\mathbf A^n_V\hookrightarrow P$, and $C\twoheadrightarrow B\twoheadrightarrow A$ is the map of $ki$.

source.place: Tag 09VD, lemma-localize-relative-pseudo-coherent, first paragraph of the proof

proof.text: The inverse-adjoining relation has an explicit two-term resolution. In the first application take $D=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, $c=a$, and $T=t$. If $(cT-1)\sum_{q=0}^N u_qT^q=0$, its constant coefficient is $-u_0=0$, and successively the coefficient of $T^q$ is $cu_{q-1}-u_q=0$, so every $u_q=0$. Together with the quotient description of step 1 this proves the exact augmented complex $0\to C\xrightarrow{at-1}C\to B\to0$. This calculation uses neither a domain assumption on $D$ nor a nonzerodivisor assumption on $c$.

source.place: Tag 09VD, proof: the polynomial-localization quotient is pseudo-coherent; explicit length-one resolution

proof.text: Apply the affine-quotient resolution sheafification theorem to $k$, the whole affine open $P$, the ideal $(at-1)$, and the augmented chain complex of step 2 (put its two terms in chain degrees $1,0$ and zero elsewhere). The required quotient-spectrum identification is exactly step 1. It gives a quasi-isomorphism from the associated two-term complex, in cochain degrees $-1,0$, to $(k_*\mathcal O_{\mathbf A^n_V})[0]$. Each term is $\mathcal O_P$: the associated sheaf of the rank-one module $C$ is the structure sheaf, as is seen on every principal open from its localization sections. Consequently this is a bounded complex of finite free sheaves and in particular a bounded-above finite free model. By the definition of absolute pseudo-coherence, $(k_*\mathcal O_{\mathbf A^n_V})[0]$ is pseudo-coherent.

source.place: Tag 09VD first paragraph; Tag 068C, lemma-regular-immersion-perfect, finite-free quotient resolution; schemes.tex Tag 01HV

proof.text: For the closed immersions used here, direct image is exact even for arbitrary module sheaves: its underlying abelian-sheaf functor is the closed-inclusion direct image, which is exact by the cited statement; kernels and cokernels of module sheaves are computed on underlying abelian sheaves with their induced module actions. Therefore on any representative complex $Rv_*=v_*$ for each such closed immersion $v$. For two composable closed immersions $v,w$, the equality $w_*v_*=(wv)_*$ follows on an open $T$ from $v^{-1}(w^{-1}T)=(wv)^{-1}T$, including the induced structure-ring action. It thus also identifies $Rw_*Rv_*$ with $R(wv)_*$. No boundedness or quasi-coherence of the representative is required.

source.place: Tag 09VA, lemma-closed-push-pseudo-coherent, opening of proof; modules.tex Tag 01AX

proof.text: Set $E'=R(ki)_*E$ on $P$. The composite $ki$ is a closed immersion. Apply the closed-pushforward pseudo-coherence equivalence to $k$ and the object $Ri_*E$: its structure-module hypothesis holds by step 3 and its input is $m$-pseudo-coherent by the hypothesis of the item. By step 4 its output $Rk_*Ri_*E$ is $E'$. Hence $E'$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent on $P$.

source.place: Tag 09VD, first paragraph: application of perfect.tex Tag 09VA

proof.text: Choose $h\in C$ mapping to $b\in A$ under the surjection in step 1. Put $W=D_P(h)=\operatorname{Spec}C_h$, using the principal-localization open immersion, and put $Q=\operatorname{Spec}C[z]=\mathbf A^{n+2}_S$. There is a surjection $C_h\twoheadrightarrow A_b$: a fraction $v/b^d$ is the image of $\widetilde v/h^d$ for any lift $\widetilde v\in C$ of $v$. It gives a closed immersion $i':U\hookrightarrow W$, whose composite with $W\hookrightarrow P$ is $(ki)|_U$, since both ring maps send each $u\in C$ to its image in $A_b$. The quotient $C[z]/(hz-1)\cong C_h$ gives a closed immersion $l:W\hookrightarrow Q$. Thus $j=li':U\hookrightarrow Q$ is a closed immersion over $S$.

source.place: Tag 09VD, second paragraph and displayed diagram

proof.text: Restrict the local strictly perfect approximations for $E'$ to $W$. Restriction to an open has the same stalks at its points, so preserves the cohomology isomorphisms above $m$ and the surjection in degree $m$; a restricted finite-free summand remains such a summand. This proves $E'|_W$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent directly from its definition. Open restriction is the sectionwise restriction functor in the cited statement, and derived open pullback is this exact functor: in the derived-pullback formula the structure-ring map is an isomorphism. On any open $T\subseteq W$, the preimage under $ki$ lies in $U$, because $h$ pulls back to $b$. Hence $((ki)_*F)|_W(T)=F((ki)^{-1}T)=(i'_*(F|_U))(T)$ for every module sheaf $F$ on $X$, with identical restriction maps and module actions. Apply this equality termwise to a representative of $E$ and use step 4 to obtain $E'|_W\cong Ri'_*(E|_U)$ in $D(\mathcal O_W)$.

source.place: Tag 09VD, second paragraph: restriction and identification with the pushforward of E restricted to U

proof.text: For $l$, repeat the coefficient calculation of step 2 with $D=C$, $c=h$, $T=z$. It gives the exact resolution $0\to C[z]\xrightarrow{hz-1}C[z]\to C_h\to0$. The affine-quotient sheafification statement applies on the whole $Q$, with ideal $(hz-1)$ and quotient-spectrum identification from step 6. As in step 3 its associated two-term complex has both terms $\mathcal O_Q$, so $(l_*\mathcal O_W)[0]$ is pseudo-coherent. Apply the closed-pushforward equivalence to $l$ and $E'|_W$, which is $m$-pseudo-coherent by step 7. It follows that $Rl_*(E'|_W)$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent. Steps 4 and 7 identify this object with $R(li')_*(E|_U)=Rj_*(E|_U)$. Taking $r=n+2$ proves the conclusion, with the given integer $m$ unchanged.

source.place: Tag 09VD, final paragraph: second application of Tag 09VA and conclusion
